item.title: Scandinavians, look here! - The Scandinavian Branch (ND) seeks recruits!: Scandinavians, look here! - The Scandinavian Branch (ND) seeks recruits!
item.content:encoded:
Hello!

We in the Scandinavian branch (ND) of the SCP Foundation are looking for new members. If you happen to speak Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, or even Faroese, you are more than welcome to come join the ND Wiki and the ND Discord server!

Because the ND branch is still in need of further development, we're especially interested in people with experience in any of the following areas:
- Moderation and Administration
- CSS coding and other technical know-how
- Translation
- Creative writing in Danish, Faroese, Norwegian, and/or Swedish

If you have experience in the two first areas (in addition to speaking one of the four languages) and wish to apply that knowledge in ND, please contact me directly with a short resume of your experiences.

Of course you're welcome as a member even if you don't already have a background in any of these areas. We need all the help we can get.
So if you're interested, come on over to http://scp-nd.wikidot.com/ and sign up!
You're also welcome to join our Discord server at: https://discord.gg/QTsMfgAu

item.title: What is your favourite SCP?: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
There are a ton of SCPs I've read, and I can't really choose a favorite out the ones I truly enjoyed but nevertheless, here are my favorites:

SCP-4205 for format-screw. Having the computer terminal display the articles and the start-up really tickled my aesthetic taste. The story of the SCP itself is not bad either, and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

SCP-5000 for story. The realization that hits you after digging deep terrifies the ever living crap out of me. Coupled with the fact that I believe in my own humanity, this SCP really brings chill down my spine and, quite frankly, I enjoy it.

SCP-001-EX for the proposal. Good boys are good, bad boys are bad. Is there anything left to say other than I liked this proposal more than the Ouroboros Cycle? Perhaps not.

Lastly, SCP-914. The experiment logs are the articles I most often come back to simply because it's a lot easier to digest.

item.title: What is your favourite SCP?: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
I really have to put another vote in here for SCP-3999. That SCP single-handedly convinced me that there's something special going on here on the wiki, and that I wanted to be part of it.

It's strange too, because it's one of the few SCPs where the particulars don't really matter. You could cut a lot from or add a lot of stuff to the first half, and it wouldn't change much. It's not some masterclass in carefully crafting the perfect word-by-word story. Yet, it has had more of an effect on how I consume fiction than any other piece of fiction.

I read it at first, and honestly tried my hardest to hate it. I tried to think that it was pretentious nonsense. But, eventually…

SCP-3999 won.

item.title: Ask The Person Above You A Question (PART IX): Re: @ Dr Talcite
item.content:encoded:
I'm rather conventional on this - Latin, and perhaps some others:
1. Those with antique writing systems that can hardly be found in today's documentations.
2. Rare, endangered derivations of a bigger language. These are often considered as "dialects", but some of them possesses enough uniqueness that can be standalone linguistically (not specialized in the field, just exemplifying)
Btw I'm already learning some constructed languages that aren't very popular. Esperanto, Lojban for instance (both less than 1 million active speakers NOW by optimistic estimation. Ephermeral existences?). And I can also use Chinese quite fluently :D
